correctness.rationale: A direct arithmetic identity reduces the connection denominator to a gcd of integers. Every order-five binary de Bruijn cycle corresponds to a 32-edge Eulerian circuit in the 16-vertex graph; all 65536 local bijections exhaust this domain, and a separate Eulerian DFS returns the identical set of exactly 2048 cycles. Both gcd implementations agree on all cycles/reversals, and the 10-value gcd and 16-value reversal-pair distributions each sum to 2048. A second pair of binary linear-complexity algorithms confirms the comparison. All complete data and executable checker are in the package. No statement beyond order five is inferred.

value.rationale: FCSR connection-denominator complexity is an established, motivated arithmetic predictability invariant; de Bruijn cycles are the canonical universal-factor family. A complete ten-level census, sharp denominator extremes, and the sixteen-class reversal joint spectrum with a maximum ratio of 1285 are naturally meaningful exact benchmarks, quantitatively distinguishing FCSR and LFSR symmetry. This is neither a mere standard gcd deduction nor an arbitrary unmotivated sample: the new content is exhaustive conditional class frequencies and their reversal behavior, certified by complete finite enumeration. No downstream cryptographic guarantee or infinite generalization is claimed.
